title: MAC vocabulary (mac_vocabulary.yaml)
description: The closed vocabularies and value domains. Governed for the same reason as everything else: a vocabulary that can grow a key nobody defined is not closed. Each block declares its kind and whether it is closed; a `vocabulary` carries `terms`, a `value_domain` carries `members`. A top-level entry is EITHER a vocabulary block or a NESTING GROUP whose children are, recursively — so `concept.column.role` may be spelled flat as one dotted key or folded as `concept: column: role:`. The DOTTED PATH is the identity either way: it is how a concept spells a value (`mac.concept.column.role.measure`), how check_vocabulary_parity names its slots, and how every generated page is addressed. The nesting is how a person reads it. Readers convert between the two in ONE place each — tools/mac_vocab.flatten here, mac_runtime.framework.Vocabulary._flatten in the platform, which cannot import across the repo boundary for the same reason both parse mac.schema.json for themselves.

canon.$comment: THE CANON BLOCK IS CONSTRAINED WHERE THE OTHERS ARE NOT, and the asymmetry is the point. A bare STRING term body is this file's normal idiom -- `concept.rule.terms.resolution`, `binding_mode.terms.restrict` and ~43 others are definitions and nothing more, so `terms` stays `{type: object}` for every other block. A CANON term is different: readers consult its fields. `serves` groups it under the pattern it exists for and is what the manual's tree is built from; `needs_sqlglot` says whether enforcing it must parse SQL; `params_from` names the parameters that must be READ from a concept rather than attached to a binding. MEASURED 2026-10-04: `ratio_select` was authored as a bare string, so it declared none of them -- it validated here, its generated section in canon_library.md silently lost its field table, and check_canon_binding._params_from() raised AttributeError on it and returned {} through a bare except, killing the attached-vs-declared check for ALL 21 canons. check_canon_documented compares term NAMES, so a name is present whether its body is a mapping or a sentence. Four readers, four reasons not to see it. This moves the refusal to the grammar, where the author can see it.

serves.description: the data pattern this canon exists for; reference_manual/patterns/<serves>.md, and the group the manual's canon tree is built from

needs_sqlglot.description: whether enforcing it must parse SQL. True makes it a guard: it catches, it does not rewrite

doc.description: what it decides, in one paragraph. The long form is reference_manual/canon/<serves>/<name>.md

params_from.description: param -> the dotted concept path it must be READ from. A parameter with a declared home must not be attached to a binding: agreeing is a restatement, disagreeing means the binding and the concept say different things and the binding is the one that runs

blockOrGroup.description: a vocabulary block, or a group of them. The group is what makes the file foldable.

members.description: members of a value_domain or registry. A `canon` member declares what it serves, whether it needs sqlglot, and — the point of params_from — which of its parameters are READABLE from a concept declaration rather than attachable to a binding.

params_from.description: canon parameter -> the dotted concept path it derives from

group.description: A NESTING GROUP — a path SEGMENT, not a vocabulary. It carries no `kind`, no `terms` and no `members`; every child is itself a block or a group. That is what keeps this from weakening the block rule: a block with a misspelled `kind` still fails BOTH branches, because as a group its children would have to be objects and a stray scalar is not one.
